name: Shelf Patchwork Tank — Open Seam
description:
Not manufactured — assembled. This tank top is the product of necessity and improvisation: panels of mismatched synth-fabric stitched together with visible seams in contrasting thread, the raw edges deliberately left open or bound in a different material entirely. Each one is unique. The one in hand might have a faded green mesh back, a yellow-white ribbed front, and shoulder straps cut from a repurposed safety harness. The stitching is uneven but functional. Shelf vendors sell them by the dozen from folded stacks under tarps.

On the Shelf, this is just a shirt. In Tier 3 clubs and underground art spaces, it's been reclaimed as aesthetic — people pay more for the 'authentic' ones than for the mass-produced knockoffs that imitate the look without the history. Real Shelf residents find that deeply irritating.
what_it_says: Either you live on the Shelf, or you want people to think you understand what that means — and those two things are not the same.
manufacturer: Various — Shelf market vendors, individual makers
story_hooks: A particular tank made from fabric cut from a Vantablack contractor's disposed uniform has been circulating the Shelf — whoever's wearing it keeps getting followed.
A Tier 3 boutique is selling machine-produced 'artisanal' versions at Φ180 and attributing them to a fictional Shelf artist — someone on the Shelf just found out.
The mismatched thread on a specific tank spells something in a old gang cipher that even the seller didn't know was there.
